title: SM Nuvali brings a new flagship mall – and traffic – to Laguna
summary: SM's 91st mall distinguishes itself with an indoor garden inspired by Singapore's Gardens by the Bay

SM's 91st mall distinguishes itself with an indoor garden inspired by Singapore's Gardens by the Bay

items: SM Nuvali, the largest mall in Laguna, officially opened on November 27, featuring a unique indoor garden and a focus on sustainability.

The mall includes various amenities such as a community library, multiple cinemas including the country's first LED cinema screens, and a curated selection of restaurants, some of which are new to the area.
Despite its grand opening, traffic congestion has already been a concern, prompting SM to coordinate with local authorities to manage traffic flow and minimize congestion for visitors.

LAGUNA, Philippines – SM has built quite a mall in the south – its biggest in Laguna, to be exact.
SM Nuvali, which officially opened its doors to the public on Friday, November 27, is a spectacle. At 190,525 square meters, it’s SM Prime’s 91st mall and the fifth in the province alone.

But this flagship mall stands apart with its sprawling air-conditioned indoor garden and a glass-paned roof to let some sunlight stream in. On the floors above, restaurants and cafés overlook the patches of green, with playgrounds and a Paw Park.

“SM Nuvali is different because it brings together nature, sustainability, and thoughtfully curated retail experiences in one destination,” SM Supermalls president Steven Tan told Rappler. “At its heart is a garden within the mall, offering an outdoor-inspired environment that is air-conditioned and designed for comfort, while being LEED-certified.”

blocks.caption: GARDEN. An indoor garden is the centerpiece of SM Nuvali. Photos by Leanne Jazul/Rappler

blocks.text: There’s a grand staircase, a community library called Book Nook with more than 10,000 books, and, on the top floor, a chapel.
Moviegoers can look forward to four regular cinemas, an IMAX auditorium with its own “IMAX Pods,” and two Director’s Club cinemas equipped with what SM calls the country’s first LED cinema screens.

blocks.caption: MOVIE. SM Nuvali features the country’s first LED cinema screens. Photo by Leanne Jazul/Rappler.

blocks.text: And though it’s new, it’s far from empty. If you’re going for food, you’ll find all the usual suspects, which Tan told Rappler was “carefully curated” – Din Tai Fung, Wildflour, Hoshino Coffee, among others – but some are showing up in Laguna for the first time, like Michelin Bib Gourmand awardee Some Thai, Golden Yolk, George & Onnie’s, and The Matcha Tokyo.
Tucked in the Food Hall is SM’s Game Park, where you can squeeze in a round of billiards or arcade games between meals.

blocks.caption: MEALS. SM Nuvali brings Makati’s Scratch smashburgers down south. Photo by Leanne Jazul/Rappler.

blocks.text: “Here, we can come together, enjoy a meal, and tell each other stories of our lives and our love,” Tan said at the mall’s opening gala on Thursday night, November 26. “We need community more than ever.”

Tan credited the Sy family “for their vision and passion to bring this development to the next level,” and then called SM Prime president Jeffrey Lim and Hans “Chico” Sy Jr. – son of Hans Sy and president of engineering, design, and development – to the stage.

blocks.caption: CHEERS! (Left to right) Hans Sy Jr., Steven Tan, and Jeffrey Lim offer a toast during the opening of SM Nuvali. Photo by Leanne Jazul/Rappler.

blocks.text: In the crowd too was Chico’s sister Hanna Carinna Sy, senior assistant vice president for marketing and leasing. The third-generation Sys are now helping to design the malls, giving the newer ones a touch of youth. And of course there was Hans Sy, who looked on like the proud father that he was. (READ: SM Harrison Plaza opening by end-2027 with entire floor for Gen Z)

“I cannot tell you enough how excited we are to welcome people to a brand new home in the South. But that will be for tomorrow,” Tan said. “So tonight, we hold this moment to ourselves and celebrate!”

blocks.caption: TYCOON. SM Prime executive committee chairman Hans Sy poses during SM Nuvali’s opening night gala. Photo by Leanne Jazul/Rappler.

blocks.text: Tomorrow, of course, means cars, and probably lots of them.

Even before the mall officially opened, motorists and residents had already been complaining online about worsening traffic along the Santa Rosa-Tagaytay Road, particularly around the traffic lights in front of the mall.

SM Nuvali sits right at the Santa Rosa-Tagaytay exit of the Cavite-Laguna Expressway (CALAX), mixing mallgoers with motorists entering and leaving the expressway. With the height of Christmas shopping season approaching, congestion could worsen even for motorists who simply use the expressway to get home or travel to Tagaytay.

Asked about the traffic situation, Tan told Rappler in a message: “We recognize the importance of managing traffic, especially with the area’s continued growth. SM Nuvali is coordinating closely with the relevant local government units and traffic authorities to support traffic management measures, including proper vehicle ingress and egress, traffic flow management, and coordination during peak hours to help minimize congestion and ensure a smoother experience for motorists and visitors.”
When Rappler visited the mall on Thursday, traffic had partly backed up to near the CALAX exit. That was before the general public could even enter the mall. – Rappler.com
